cwe.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

license: Original code written for Exhibit A; no third-party code vendored (see README.md).
note: Self-contained Node oracle case (Express, node:test, no replay): proven directly with effect='canary_read' once the Node oracle (T125) judges it. No upstream repo/commit applies: the code is an original reimplementation of the vulnerable download pattern, not Express itself.

real_world_analog.fix: express.static and res.sendFile validate the resolved path against the root before serving it; the fixed tree does the same with an original path.normalize containment check.
real_world_analog.summary: Directory traversal in Express static file serving: the requested path was resolved with no check that it stayed inside the served root, so '..' segments read arbitrary files. The same dangerous pattern recurs whenever res.sendFile is handed a user-controlled path.
real_world_analog.verification: Advisory id and summary confirmed via the Express security-updates page in a web search on 2026-11-01; the app in this case is original code written from that pattern, not Express.

bypass.expectation: proven against fixed_incomplete: the dots are percent-encoded, so the screen on the raw request text sees no '..' segment and the name is decoded and resolved afterwards; the incomplete fix must not be accepted as fixed.
